{
  "candidate_rtl": "module pw_alu #(
    parameter WIDTH = 64
)(
    input wire [WIDTH-1:0] a, b,
    input wire [2:0] Oper,
    output reg [WIDTH-1:0] sum
);
    wire [WIDTH-1:0] x;
    wire [WIDTH-1:0] add_g, ab_g, ba_g;
    wire [WIDTH-1:0] add_c, ab_c, ba_c;
    wire [WIDTH-1:0] add_result, ab_result, ba_result;
    wire sel_add, sel_ab, sel_ba;
    wire sel_or, sel_and, sel_xor, sel_xnor;

    assign x = a ^ b;
    assign add_g = a & b;
    assign ab_g = (~a) & b;
    assign ba_g = a & (~b);

    pw_alu_carry4 #(.WIDTH(WIDTH)) u_add (
        .p(x), .g(add_g), .c(add_c)
    );
    pw_alu_carry4 #(.WIDTH(WIDTH)) u_ab (
        .p(~x), .g(ab_g), .c(ab_c)
    );
    pw_alu_carry4 #(.WIDTH(WIDTH)) u_ba (
        .p(~x), .g(ba_g), .c(ba_c)
    );

    assign add_result = x ^ add_c;
    assign ab_result = x ^ ab_c;
    assign ba_result = x ^ ba_c;

    assign sel_add  = (Oper == 3'b000);
    assign sel_ab   = (Oper == 3'b001);
    assign sel_ba   = (Oper == 3'b010);
    assign sel_or   = (Oper == 3'b011);
    assign sel_and  = (Oper == 3'b100);
    assign sel_xor  = (Oper == 3'b101);
    assign sel_xnor = (Oper == 3'b110);

    always @* begin
        sum = ({WIDTH{sel_add}} & add_result)
            | ({WIDTH{sel_ab}} & ab_result)
            | ({WIDTH{sel_ba}} & ba_result)
            | ({WIDTH{sel_or}} & (a | b))
            | ({WIDTH{sel_and}} & (a & b))
            | ({WIDTH{sel_xor}} & x)
            | ({WIDTH{sel_xnor}} & (~x));
    end
endmodule

module pw_alu_carry4 #(
    parameter WIDTH = 64
)(
    input wire [WIDTH-1:0] p,
    input wire [WIDTH-1:0] g,
    output wire [WIDTH-1:0] c
);
    localparam BLOCKS = (WIDTH + 3) / 4;
    localparam PAD_WIDTH = 4 * BLOCKS;
    localparam LEVELS = $clog2(BLOCKS);

    wire [PAD_WIDTH-1:0] pp, gg;
    wire [BLOCKS-1:0] bp [0:LEVELS];
    wire [BLOCKS-1:0] bg [0:LEVELS];
    wire [BLOCKS-1:0] block_c;

    genvar i, j, s;
    generate
        for (i = 0; i < PAD_WIDTH; i = i + 1) begin: padding
            if (i < WIDTH) begin: real_bit
                assign pp[i] = p[i];
                assign gg[i] = g[i];
            end else begin: neutral_bit
                assign pp[i] = 1'b1;
                assign gg[i] = 1'b0;
            end
        end

        for (j = 0; j < BLOCKS; j = j + 1) begin: groups
            assign bp[0][j] = &pp[4*j +: 4];
            assign bg[0][j] = gg[4*j+3]
                | (pp[4*j+3] & gg[4*j+2])
                | (pp[4*j+3] & pp[4*j+2] & gg[4*j+1])
                | (pp[4*j+3] & pp[4*j+2] & pp[4*j+1] & gg[4*j]);
        end

        for (s = 0; s < LEVELS; s = s + 1) begin: prefix_level
            for (j = 0; j < BLOCKS; j = j + 1) begin: prefix_node
                if (j >= (1 << s)) begin: combine
                    assign bp[s+1][j] = bp[s][j] & bp[s][j-(1 << s)];
                    assign bg[s+1][j] = bg[s][j]
                        | (bp[s][j] & bg[s][j-(1 << s)]);
                end else begin: pass
                    assign bp[s+1][j] = bp[s][j];
                    assign bg[s+1][j] = bg[s][j];
                end
            end
        end

        for (j = 0; j < BLOCKS; j = j + 1) begin: block_inputs
            if (j == 0) begin: first
                assign block_c[j] = 1'b0;
            end else begin: later
                assign block_c[j] = bg[LEVELS][j-1];
            end
        end

        for (i = 0; i < WIDTH; i = i + 1) begin: local_carries
            if ((i % 4) == 0) begin: bit0
                assign c[i] = block_c[i/4];
            end else if ((i % 4) == 1) begin: bit1
                assign c[i] = gg[i-1]
                    | (pp[i-1] & block_c[i/4]);
            end else if ((i % 4) == 2) begin: bit2
                assign c[i] = gg[i-1]
                    | (pp[i-1] & gg[i-2])
                    | (pp[i-1] & pp[i-2] & block_c[i/4]);
            end else begin: bit3
                assign c[i] = gg[i-1]
                    | (pp[i-1] & gg[i-2])
                    | (pp[i-1] & pp[i-2] & gg[i-3])
                    | (pp[i-1] & pp[i-2] & pp[i-3] & block_c[i/4]);
            end
        end
    endgenerate
endmodule
",
  "bottleneck": "The reported critical paths run from lower operand bits to upper result bits through many mapped logic stages. Arithmetic carry or borrow propagation followed by operation selection is the principal optimization target; exact source attribution cannot be established from the mapped names alone.",
  "rewrite": "Replace inferred arithmetic with parallel four-bit-group carry and borrow lookahead networks. Group carries use a logarithmic parallel-prefix tree, while carries within each group use expanded lookahead equations. Addition and both subtraction directions share the operand XOR. Subtractions directly propagate borrow, avoiding operand inversion and a carry-in-one path. Mutually exclusive operation masks select the results in parallel.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "At WIDTH=32, each arithmetic network has eight four-bit groups and three group-prefix levels, followed by local lookahead, result XOR, and output selection. This targets a shorter critical path than the measured 2.49 ns baseline. The actual gain requires synthesis and STA with the specified mapping and constraints; no new timing result is claimed.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "Three parallel arithmetic networks trade carry-network wiring and lookahead logic for timing. Shared XOR, shared subtraction propagation, and synthesis elimination of unused carry outputs limit overhead. Compliance with the 6534.767360 um2 area cap and library electrical limits requires mapped evaluation and is not claimed as measured.",
  "functional_boundaries": "Pure combinational, unsigned, WIDTH-bit behavior is preserved for all binary inputs: 000 adds, 001 computes a-b, 010 computes b-a, 011 ORs, 100 ANDs, 101 XORs, 110 XNORs, and 111 returns zero. Arithmetic overflow and final borrow are discarded. The default WIDTH remains 64, with WIDTH=32 supported without specialization; positive non-multiple-of-four widths use neutral padding. No state, latency, assumptions, undefined outputs, or external dependencies are introduced. The supplied module has no CRC ports or state."
